title: Evelyn #1
description:
Hello everyone! I'm glad you're following my work.

- How do I change the wallpaper color? --

Wallpaper Engine has a built-in feature called "Show Color Settings." Your translation may differ slightly. This feature is located under the preview of my work in the app itself. Clicking on this line reveals four sliders that control the tint, color, and brightness of the work. You need the "Tint" slider. This will allow you to change the color of the work.

- How do I change the effects of my work? --

Under my preview, specifically in the "Color Settings" section I mentioned above, there's a list of effects with blue squares next to them. Clicking on them toggles specific effects on and off.

title: Spectrum City Audio Visualizer
description:
(2025.8.24 update)

Fixed a 2D rotation bug. The bug: the 2D rotation could get reset after changing the canvas position or restarting, which also messed up the 2D XY position.

Also added a slight glow to the clock.

(2025.8.19 initial submit)

There are lots of settings I added to make this as playable as possible. I had to remind myself not to add more, or this wallpaper would probably never get released.

Must-try settings:

- Bar Colors: hue

The "Waterfall" settings usually only look good when the anti-aliasing is on — otherwise it might look weird. These settings are for a preset I’ll be releasing soon, called “Spectrum Audio Visualizer But It's Waterfall.”
(It's now published: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3553186925)

When the flow anti-aliasing is turned off, the flow only moves from one pixel to another — in other words, from lattice point to lattice point. In this mode, if the flow velocity is small, the number of possible flow directions becomes very limited. For example, to move at a clean 45° angle it would need a velocity vector like (1,1), which means the velocity has to have a norm of at least √2.

When I first developed this wallpaper, all rotations were zero and the flow just moved straight upward. That basically turned the audio visualizer into a spectrogram, which was originally what I intended. (I forgot the terminology so that the name became spectrum visualizer). But after playing around with it, I ended up publishing it with a default preset that makes it look like buildings in a night city because it looks cute. Maybe the hue or background color could still use some tweaking, but I’ll probably leave it as-is.
